evidence_items.summary: Identifying subtle errors in generated videos is an important step toward automated video generation, where errors must be detected to assess and refine generated clips. Recent work shows that pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) can localise such errors, but their effectiveness depends strongly on the workflow used: choices about which frames to inspect, which tools and model calls to make, and how to combine predictions can lead to substantially different results. We study VLM harnesses for video error localisation. Instead of relying on manually designed harnesses, we propose Harness Search and Merge (HSM), an algorithm that automatically constructs them by searching over executable evaluation programs. An LLM orchestrator refines candidate harnesses independently on random training subsets, records findings in a memory, and constructively merges complementary candidates. We evaluate HSM on Spotlight, a recently proposed benchmark for localising errors in generated videos. HSM achieves 0.234 $\pm$ 0.012 F1, exceeding the strongest benchmark strategy (0.173 $\pm$ 0.016), and retains its lead on an unseen video generator (0.213 $\pm$ 0.008 versus 0.140 $\pm$ 0.003). On IPV-Bench, it achieves strong localisation performance with lower false-alarm rates than existing optimisation baselines. Together, these results show that searching over complete VLM harnesses can outperform existing evaluation strategies, transfer to an unseen video generator, and reduce false alarms on real videos.
evidence_items.title: Optimising VLM Harnesses to Localise Errors in Generated Videos

evidence_items.summary: Proactive streaming video understanding requires models to interpret unfolding events, respond timely, and retrieve relevant historical evidence. To systematically evaluate these capabilities, we introduce SVUBench, a comprehensive proactive streaming video benchmark comprising 12,131 questions and 62,881 answer points across ten proactive tasks spanning Perception, Understanding, and Reasoning. Constructed through model-assisted annotation and human verification, SVUBench introduces two complementary interaction modes. Basic evaluates sustained proactive responses from video onset, while Trajectory requires historical recovery and continuous response updates following task activation during streaming. A Duration-Scaled Challenge further evaluates these capabilities across four video duration tiers. We develop the Proactive Response Score (PRS) with task-adaptive answer windows to jointly assess answer correctness, response timeliness, historical consistency, and content quality. Extensive experiments and analysis reveal the strengths and limitations of existing models, highlighting directions for advancing proactive streaming video understanding.
evidence_items.title: SVUBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding

evidence_items.summary: A Large Language Model (LLM), its harness, and the test-time compute budget jointly determine its behavior. Consequently, the same underlying model, embedded in different agentic workflows or allocated different amounts of test-time compute, can exhibit markedly different performance. Psychologists face an analogous challenge when evaluating human performance: the same person may behave differently under different incentives and levels of deliberation. Psychological tasks therefore provide an ideal testbed for studying such behavioral variation. However, when adapted to LLMs, these tasks are typically text-transcribed, replaying fixed, language-rendered experiments as static prompts. This format is ill-suited to agent evaluation, where actions can alter future observations and task states. Conversely, although dynamic environments are prevalent in the evaluation of LLM agents, they rarely ask whether the resulting behavior is human-like. Here, we bridge this gap by transforming psychological tasks into dynamic environments in which agents can interact and by using a learned human-policy model to evaluate how compatible the resulting behavioral trajectories are with human behavior. Across these environments, we find that this compatibility varies with an LLM's agentic configuration and the psychological task, and that memory raises it mainly by making choices more predictable rather than more human-like. These findings motivate a more holistic evaluation of LLM agents in psychology-inspired environments, accounting for both the backbone model and its agentic scaffold.
evidence_items.title: mini-psych-agent: Evaluating Human-Like Behavior in LLM Agents through Interactive Psychological Environments

evidence_items.summary: Ranking functions are a fundamental technique for proving loop termination, but synthesizing them remains challenging and often requires substantial expertise. Despite considerable progress in their automated synthesis, existing approaches remain limited in their effectiveness. We propose RAINFALL, a neuro-symbolic framework that tightly integrates large language models (LLMs) with symbolic verification. To our best knowledge, RAINFALL is the first to employ a generate-verify-refine paradigm for LLM-based ranking function synthesis. RAINFALL formulates ranking function synthesis as a constrained code-completion task, inserting placeholders into the input program that the LLM must fill in four predefined slots per loop. The resulting program is checked by a symbolic verifier. Successful verification yields a valid ranking function, while verification failures produce diagnostics that are translated into natural-language feedback to guide iterative refinement. We evaluate RAINFALL on two public benchmark suites comprising 358 terminating C programs. Using DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, RAINFALL synthesizes verified ranking functions for 333 programs (93.02%), outperforming all evaluated baselines. Notably, it solves 22 more programs than PROTON 2.1, the winner of the SV-COMP 2026 Termination Category. Combining RAINFALL with PROTON 2.1 further increases the success rate to 96.65% (346/358 programs). Ablation studies demonstrate the contributions of placeholder contracts, few-shot examples, symbolic verification, and diagnostic feedback, while experiments across different LLMs establish the broader applicability of the framework.
evidence_items.title: Ranking Function Generation with LLMs for Termination

evidence_items.summary: Agent benchmarks test what agents can do in environments that are built for their tasks. Deployed agents work in the real world where other people and tools can change the state. An agent booking a flight may receive a message from someone else to change the destination, or a booking tool may fail without saying whether the ticket was purchased. We present BACKDROP, which asks how much of an agent's capability in a clean world survives in a non-cooperative world. BACKDROP takes a task along with the agent's execution environment, and plants four everyday hazards in its environment, one at a time and all together. Each hazard tests a different behavior. Authority: does a non-author actor instruction, from anyone who did not author the task, override the user's goal? Injection: does text planted in a record redirect the agent? Boundary: does the agent make changes in an app the user's task did not require? Fault: after a write fails without saying whether it landed, does the agent check before it retries? Across 3,678 variants and 16 models, the average pass rate falls from 69.5% to 31.3% once all four hazards are present; the strongest models fall furthest (Claude Fable 5.1 from 96.6% to 56.0%). The gap is consistent throughout all 16 models. BACKDROP formalizes these gaps and shows how an agent's score in a task's world is a ceiling on real-world performance.
evidence_items.title: Exploring the Hidden Cost of the World Around AI Agents

evidence_items.summary: Large multimodal models (LMMs) have demonstrated strong OCR recognition capabilities, yet remain vulnerable to adversarial visual text that is readable to humans but challenging for models to localize and recognize. Existing OCR benchmarks mainly focus on natural or document-style text, while adversarial OCR evaluations remain limited in scale, task coverage, or region-aware evaluation. In this paper, we formulate adversarial OCR as a \textbf{grounded OCR perception} task and introduce \textbf{AdvSpot}, the first benchmark for grounded adversarial OCR evaluation. AdvSpot comprises 383 images with region-level annotations, spanning 5 primary categories and 13 fine-grained adversarial OCR types. To address this challenge, we propose \textbf{ArmorOCR}, a two-stage training framework for robust adversarial OCR perception. ArmorOCR first acquires missing adversarial OCR perception from privileged transformed observations through On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), and then refines grounded OCR perception through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with task-conditioned rewards for localization, recognition, full spotting, and visual question answering (VQA). Experiments on our AdvSpot, other adversarial OCR benchmarks, and general OCR benchmarks demonstrate that ArmorOCR consistently improves adversarial OCR perception while preserving competitive general OCR capability. The benchmark and code are available at https://github.com/ant-research/ArmorOCR
evidence_items.title: ArmorOCR: Grounded Adversarial Visual Perception via Observation-Transferred Self-Distillation

evidence_items.summary: Text-to-CAD has recently emerged as an important task with the potential to substantially accelerate design workflows. Despite its significance, there has been surprisingly little work on Text-to-CAD evaluation, and assessing CAD model generation performance remains a considerable challenge. In this work, we introduce a new evaluation perspective for Text-to-CAD based on automated testing. We propose CADTestBench, the first test-based benchmark for Text-to-CAD, based on CADTests, executable software tests that verify whether a generated CAD model satisfies the geometric and topological requirements of the input prompt. Using CADTestBench, we conduct comprehensive benchmarking of recent Text-to-CAD methods and further demonstrate that CADTests can also guide CAD model generation, yielding simple baselines that surpass performance of current methods. CADTestBench code and data are available.
evidence_items.title: Text-to-CAD Evaluation with CADTests

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to extract information from electronic health records (EHRs). Given the rapid pace of LLM development, robust scenario-specific benchmarks are essential to evaluate clinical usefulness and support safe deployment. Objective This study aimed to compare contemporary LLMs for structured data extraction from real neurosurgical EHRs written in Czech. Methods In a prospective single-center cohort, 172 hospitalized patients provided informed consent for the use of anonymized EHRs. For each patient, predefined records were collected and concatenated. Ground truth for 35 data points was established by dual extraction with consensus. A standardized prompt requesting JSON output was submitted to 19 LLMs. The primary outcome was overall accuracy; secondary outcomes were category-level accuracy and the proportion of complete machine-readable outputs. Results A total of 6264 documents were collected (median 33, IQR 25-41 per patient). Ground truth was established with 92.6% initial interrater agreement before consensus. Several models produced complete JSON outputs for 100% of cases (Claude 4.1 Opus, Grok 4, and Gemini 2.5 Flash); GPT-4.1 (DeepSearch) and GPT-5 completed 99.4%. The highest accuracy was achieved by GPT-4.1 (87.6%), followed by GPT-4.5 (85.6%), Claude 4.1 (84.8%), and Grok 4 (84.2%). Accuracy declined by data type: binary (up to 95%), numeric (~89%), multiple-choice (~75%), and short text (~78%). Conclusions Current LLMs can reliably extract structured clinical information from full, non-English EHRs, while older or smaller models show major limitations. A hybrid workflow—automated extraction with targeted validation—appears practical for research use.
evidence_items.title: Large Language Model Performance in Structured Data Extraction From Neurosurgical Electronic Health Records: Comparative Benchmark Study
Know2Guess: A Contamination-Aware Multi-zone Benchmark for Knowledge-Boundary Evaluation in Large Language Models

organizations: Department of Nutrition and Dietetics, Faculty of Health Sciences, Istanbul Gelisim University , Istanbul ,
Department of Nutrition and Dietetics, Faculty of Health Sciences, Bursa Uludag University , Bursa ,
evidence_items.summary: Abstract Health-oriented claims on nutritionally unfavourable foods may create misleading perceptions of overall healthfulness. This cross-sectional benchmark study evaluated three large language models (Grok-4.6, Gemini-3.7, and ChatGPT-5.6) in identifying nutrition and health claims and detecting potential health-halo marketing on packaged foods. Of 1,666 products screened, 1,606 with complete ingredient and nutrition information were included. Two trained dietitians independently assigned NOVA categories and Nutri-Score grades, with consensus classifications used as the reference standard. Health-halo marketing was defined as at least one healthfulness-related front-of-pack claim on a Nutri-Score D or E product. Overall, 162 products (10.1%) carried claims; 77.8% of products with calculable Nutri-Scores were graded D or E, and 83.3% were NOVA 4. Among claim-bearing products, 72 (44.4%) met the health-halo definition. ChatGPT-5.6 achieved the best claim identification (exact-set accuracy = 47.5%; micro-F1 = 0.632), Nutri-Score agreement (weighted κ = 0.895), and balanced health-halo detection (sensitivity = 86.1%; specificity = 75.9%; F1 = 0.800). Gemini-3.7 performed best for NOVA classification (accuracy = 90.6%; κ = 0.693) but showed low health-halo specificity (17.2%). Grok-4.6 demonstrated limited health-halo discrimination (F1 = 0.265). Performance varied substantially across tasks, precluding unsupervised regulatory or public-health surveillance use.
evidence_items.title: Can Large Language Models Detect Health-Halo Marketing on Packaged Foods? A Regulatory and Nutrient-Profile Benchmark Study

organizations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, School of Computer Science
evidence_items.summary: This paper presents a comprehensive survey of different researchs on large language model text watermarking. This survey reads 29 related works in depth and organises the field by the place where the watermark enters the generation pipeline: the model's weights, the decoding step, or a rewrite of text outside the model, subdividing decoding-time schemes by the mechanism that carries the signal. It argues that the insertion point can be viewed the one of the most important properties, deciding a scheme's detector requirements, its attack surface, and the deployment settings open to it. Additionally, this survey summarizes existing watermark attacks, which are organised by adversarial operation and quantified budget, from paraphrasing and translation to text mixing, key stealing, and model distillation. Because the three benchmarks surveyed are based on mutually incompatible axes, no cross-paper ranking is reported here. Finally, this paper concludes the key open challenges in current research and possible future research directions. This survey intends to provide researchers and engineering practitioners with a concise, systematic and in-depth understanding of the latest progress in LLM watermarking, and further facilitate the development of trustworthy generative artificial intelligence systems.
evidence_items.title: Large language model watermarking: a survey of techniques, attacks, evaluation, and future directions

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Informal caregivers of older adults with Alzheimer disease and related dementias (ADRD) often face high burden and chronic stress. Reddit provides naturally occurring caregiver narratives to study caregiving burden, but prior studies have often relied on small manual coding or aggregate topic models that may not easily connect caregiving context, burden, and stressors at scale. Objective This study aimed to explore what a large language model (LLM)–assisted measurement workflow can recover from ADRD caregiving-related Reddit discourse, such as caregiver burden, caregiving contexts, stressors, temporal patterns, and high-burden subgroups. Methods We processed monthly Reddit submission archives from January 2020 through June 2025. Posts were selected from 5 ADRD-specific subreddits and 4 broader caregiving or aging subreddits, yielding a balanced 13,200-post corpus. A locally hosted open-weight LLM inferred structured post-level variables, including caregiver sociodemographic characteristics, caregiver role, ADRD stage, care setting, support need, dominant emotion, sentiment, burden, and primary and secondary stressors. The workflow included schema validation, uncertainty ratings, field-level correction prompts, source matching, a 150-post double-coded human validation benchmark, and pairwise subgroup analyses. Results The source-matched analytic sample included 13,179 LLM-coded posts. Human agreement was high for caregiver role, ADRD stage, care setting, dominant emotion, support need type, burden group, and stressor categories (Cohen κ=0.77-1.00), but poor for the initial in-scope screen (κ=0.00). Adult children were the largest inferred caregiver group (8,266/13,179, 62.7%), followed by grandchildren (2,012/13,179, 15.3%). Moderate ADRD was the modal inferred stage (6,554/13,179, 49.7%), and home was the modal care setting (7,145/13,179, 54.2%).
evidence_items.title: Alzheimer Disease and Related Dementias Caregiver Burden on Reddit: Large Language Model–Assisted Measurement Study

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in generating virtual patients for health care applications. However, whether LLM-generated virtual patients can reproduce patient-reported priority rankings remains uncertain. Objective We evaluated whether LLM-generated virtual hypertension patients could approximate real patient-reported perspectives, and whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improved alignment with patient-reported priority rankings. Methods A total of 20 patients from multiple regions completed structured questionnaires ranking priorities across 7 domains related to AI-assisted hypertension management. A total of 8 LLMs were evaluated under 3 simulation conditions: unconstrained generation, patient-specific simulation, and RAG-enhanced simulation. For unconstrained generation, each model produced 20 virtual patient profiles, each constructed by grouping baseline variables into the study categories and selecting the most frequent category across 10 repeated generations. For patient-specific baseline and RAG-enhanced simulations, each model generated 10 complete questionnaire responses per participant and condition; the modal complete 4-item ranking within each domain was selected as the final ranking. Model-generated rankings were compared with patient-reported rankings using total accuracy, top-1 accuracy, and full accuracy. In addition, 5 hypertension clinicians independently inferred patient-priority rankings while blinded to both real patient responses and LLM outputs, providing a human reference benchmark. Results Aggregated unconstrained virtual patient profiles varied across models, with 45%‐55% having college-level education, and 75%‐95% using antihypertensive medication. In patient-specific baseline simulations, total accuracy ranged from 46.3% to 71.4%.
evidence_items.title: Evaluating Large Language Model–Generated Virtual Hypertension Patients as Proxies for Real Patient Perspectives: Comparative Study

organizations: Bharati Vidyapeeth's College of Engineering, Delhi
evidence_items.summary: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit a specific and previously undercharacterised reasoning failure we term symbolic drift hallucination: an intermediate variable within a multi-step computation graph silently receives an incorrect value, which then propagates through all subsequent derivations to yield an output that is linguistically coherent, structurally sound, and numerically wrong. This failure mode is invisible to existing single-signal verifiers because the model’s verbally stated answer and its generated symbolic code both carry the same corrupted value, causing them to agree on an incorrect result. We present HalluciNOT (Hallucination Neutralisation via Obligatory Testing), a three-stage post-hoc framework comprising: a constrained Program-of-Thought equation generator that enforces structural integrity of symbolic outputs; a guarded drift detector that compares sandboxed execution results against the ground truth, closing the detection gap that defeats verifiers restricted to the model’s own outputs; and a targeted Reflexion repair loop that isolates the corrupted variable for re-grounding. Because the repair stage accepts a candidate only when it lies within $$10^{-6}$$ of the ground truth, a strictly tighter bound than the $$10^{-3}$$ tolerance of the evaluation metric, the framework cannot convert a correct result into an incorrect one; the guarantee is unconditional, independent of repair quality, and independent of detector calibration. This framework is scoped to contexts where ground truth is available at inference time, such as automated grading, evaluation pipelines, and educational platforms with known answer keys. Evaluated on 600 samples across three benchmarks (GSM-Hard, SVAMP, and MAWPS, each with $$n = 200),$$ HalluciNOT achieves accuracy of 92.0%, 99.5%, and 100.0% respectively, with gains of +23.0, +4.0, and +5.5 percentage points over the LLM baseline.
evidence_items.title: HalluciNOT: execution grounded detection and targeted repair of symbolic drift hallucinations in large language model reasoning

evidence_items.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have drawn more research interest in construction safety inspection recently due to their capacity to integrate visual understanding, language understanding, and reasoning. In this paper, a survey is conducted to review the recent research on MLLMs in construction safety inspection, covering techniques, datasets, evaluation, applications, and limitations. The current studies primarily utilize prompt-based adaptation and in-context learning, domain-specific fine-tuning, and knowledge-augmented reasoning to enhance the performance of MLLMs in the construction domain. Applications of MLLMs in construction safety inspection include hazard detection and localization, safety inspection, visual question answering, assistance, and report generation. From the current studies, it can be found that MLLMs can be used to perform flexible and interpretable analysis for construction safety inspection with the assistance of domain knowledge and prompts. Nevertheless, the limitations of MLLMs in construction safety inspection are still present, such as poor visual grounding and spatial reasoning, lack of domain knowledge, lack of large and balanced datasets, and uncertainty of application in real-world scenarios. For the future work, it is recommended to enhance multimodal grounding, construct a larger and more balanced dataset in the construction domain, integrate safety regulations in a trustworthy manner, and perform human validation systematically. MLLMs have great potential to be applied in construction safety inspection; however, they can be used as decision aids rather than replacements for safety inspectors at present.
evidence_items.title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Construction Safety Inspection
A High-Frequency Snapshot Dataset and Benchmark for Early Prediction of YouTube Shorts Virality

evidence_items.summary: Objective: The Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD) provides expert-curated chemical-gene interactions about environmental exposure effects on human diseases. Existing automated relation extraction systems are typically restricted to 3-10 interaction types and operate on abstracts only. We introduce CLOVER, a systematic benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) on full-text chemical-gene interaction extraction using CTD-defined chemical-gene interaction terminology. The framework is designed to support 47 base interactions with directional modifiers (increase, decrease, affects), yielding 136 possible supported interaction classes. Evaluation is restricted to the subset of classes represented in the selected articles. Methods: CLOVER processes 50 full-text PubMed Central articles (1,563 sections) with PubTator and CTD integration. The pipeline consists of four stages: (1) LLM Extraction with one-shot and few-shot prompting; (2) LLM Validation to confirm and revise interactions; (3) Rule-based Refinement of extracted interactions to standardize terminology and eliminate errors; and (4) Human Review for expert oversight. We benchmark four LLMs (GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) and compare against a naive baseline that applies unstructured prompting directly to full-text PDFs. Results: The naive baseline achieves only 13% recall and 36% precision. Refinement significantly enhances performance by eliminating unsupported interactions. Under strict limitations, Claude-Sonnet-4.5 alone achieves 72% recall and 61% precision, and Claude with self-validation achieves 74% recall and 49% precision compared to CTD. Of the 136 supported interaction classes, 17 were represented in our evaluation. Conclusion: To our knowledge, CLOVER establishes the first benchmark for full-text chemical-gene interaction extraction aligned with CTD.
evidence_items.title: CLOVER: Chemical-gene LLM benchmark for obtaining valid entity relationships for the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD)

organizations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
evidence_items.summary: Recent advances in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics have enabled high-resolution characterization of gene expression and cellular organization in situ. Resolving within-cell-type heterogeneity is essential for understanding how cellular states relate to tissue function and disease. However, imperfect cell segmentation and RNA spillover can contaminate cell-level expression profiles, obscuring intrinsic expression patterns and generating spurious variation. Existing decontamination methods can struggle to distinguish intrinsic variation from contamination when both are inferred from spatial measurements alone, and may suppress genuine state-associated signals when within-cell-type heterogeneity is not explicitly modeled. Here we present Dancer, a reference-guided probabilistic framework that disentangles within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination by combining cell-type-specific gene programs learned from single-cell data with explicit modeling of intrinsic expression, neighboring-cell contamination and background RNA. Across multiple human tumor datasets with varying gene compositions and panel sizes, Dancer improves cell-type separation and expression specificity while preserving identity-associated signals, achieving superior overall performance in benchmark comparisons. Inferred gene program activities reveal within-cell-type heterogeneity in the form of distinct cellular states and continuous spatial gradients associated with local tissue environments, while reference-guided panel expansion extends molecular characterization beyond the measured genes. Together, Dancer supports accurate transcript decontamination and more faithful interpretation of cellular heterogeneity within its native tissue context.
evidence_items.title: Disentangling within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics

organizations: Graduate Program in Systems and Computer Engineering (PESC), COPPE, Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro 21941-914, Brazil
Department of Computer Science, Toronto Metropolitan University, Toronto, ON M5B-2K3, Canada
evidence_items.summary: Evaluating lay-facing health guidance from Large Language Models (LLMs) in the Global South requires human-centered explainability (HCXAI) tailored to local health systems and vulnerable populations. We introduce HCXAI-BR, a reproducible evaluation protocol featuring a five-axis, behaviorally anchored rubric—Safety, Accessible Language, Local Contextualization, Contestability, and Transparency—applied to 15 low-risk health scenarios in Brazilian Portuguese. In a pilot model-identity-masked evaluation of six global and national LLMs (90 responses), top-tier global proprietary and adapted commercial models achieved comparable performance (GPT-5.6 Luna 7.33/10, Sabiá-4 BR-SP 7.03/10, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite 6.83/10), outperforming the national open-weight models, even on local contextualization within Brazil’s public health network (SUS/UBS). These pilot-scale comparisons, from fifteen prompts and a single response per model, demonstrate the protocol’s ability to discriminate between models, not a statistically validated ranking. An instrument-diagnostic pass resolved conceptual ambiguities between safety directives and epistemic humility, improving contestability inter-rater agreement (κ = 0.485). Our findings demonstrate that post-training alignment of capable base models offers a more viable path toward human-centered, sovereign AI in resource-constrained health ecosystems than small-scale pre-training from scratch. This single, confounded comparison (parameter count and training budget differ between the two models) should be read as a provisional, exploratory observation rather than a general, statistically established claim. SUS and UBS, used above, abbreviate Brazil’s Unified Health System (Sistema Único de Saúde) and its primary-care clinics (Unidades Básicas de Saúde), respectively.
evidence_items.title: HCXAI-BR: A Reproducible Benchmark for Human-Centered Explainability and Contestability in Brazilian Health Information Guidance

organizations: School of Computer, Hubei Polytechnic University
School of Power and Energy, Nanchang Hangkong University
evidence_items.summary: Neuroimaging studies increasingly combine brain measurements with multiple clinical scales, yet prediction remains difficult when a new subject has imaging data but an incomplete clinical profile. Standard PARAFAC is transductive: it learns one subject-factor row for each training subject and has no direct mechanism for a held-out subject without fold-in or model refitting. We introduce SI-PARAFAC, a side-information-guided extension that replaces this lookup table with a learned attribute-to-factor mapping. A multi-layer perceptron (MLP) maps functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) measurements from 108 anatomical brain regions defined by the Automated Anatomical Labeling (AAL) atlas to subject factors, whereas the clinical-variable and AAL-region factors retain the standard PARAFAC form. We evaluated the method on 70 subjects with 108 AAL-region fMRI measurements and 15 clinical variables, several of which had substantial missingness. In the reported 5-fold subject-level analysis, SI-MLP achieved lower cold-start RMSE than a direct MLP regressor (0.6736 versus 1.1503) and lower warm-start RMSE than standard PARAFAC (0.3686 versus 0.3946). A nested rank-selection experiment yielded a cold-start RMSE of 0.6883 ± 0.0534 and selected R = 15 in 50.0% of outer folds. Standard PARAFAC with post-hoc fold-in rules was competitive or better, with ridge fold-in reaching 0.6309. These findings indicate that AAL-region fMRI features can support held-out-subject prediction while preserving the clinical-variable-by-AAL-region tensor structure, although larger multi-site studies are required to assess external generalization.
evidence_items.title: Cold-start prediction of depression clinical profiles from neuroimaging: a systematic benchmark of attribute-guided tensor factorization

evidence_items.summary: As AI agents increasingly assist people across digital and physical settings, evidence about individuals accumulates through digital interactions and observations of physical-world activities. When multiple agents maintain separate personal contexts, knowledge about the same person can become fragmented, making it difficult to maintain continuity and user control. We argue that personal AI should instead be organized around a shared personal representation under the individual's control. We propose Personal Agentic Twin, a three-plane architecture that connects distributed evidence to an evolving private twin of the individual, from which purpose-specific scoped twins draw personal knowledge to provide assistance and act on the individual's behalf. Authorization and execution controls link the personal knowledge available to each scoped twin with the actions it is allowed to take and the updates it can propose. We illustrate the architecture through representative application scenarios and call for research on the methods and evaluations needed to realize this vision. Personal Agentic Twin offers a foundation for personal AI that extends people's capabilities while preserving their authority over how they are represented and how agents act on their behalf.
evidence_items.title: Personal Agentic Twin: User-Controlled Memory and Policy-Scoped Representations for Agentic AI

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Formation evaluation depends as much on judgement — which minerals are present, which log response has a cause the model does not assume, when the agreement with independent data is good enough — as on equations. We describe how an agentic system encodes that judgement in reusable skills and couples it to server-side petrophysical computation. A skill is a reviewed procedure with structured triggers, input requirements, an ordered evidence hierarchy, a loop with permitted moves, a convergence gate and a stop rule, plus reference documents loaded only when a symptom calls for them. We dissect fe-mineral-inversion, the skill that runs a calibrated multi-mineral inversion, and contrast it with a display skill that renders logs without passing curve data through the language model. The harness runs a generic plan–act–observe–check loop; the skill supplies the thresholds, moves and stop rule; and a wellbore computation service reached through the Model Context Protocol (142 methods in 18 groups) produces every number. On Antelope 1-36-25H, a Madison Group well in the Williston Basin, a carbonate interpretation without halite reported 386.5 ft of pay; an evaporite-masked chain reduced this to 101.5 ft, and Madison Group pay fell from 309.5 to 52.0 ft. The calibration loop reduced the mean reconstruction error from 3.44 to 0.51 in two self-diagnosed steps — adding halite, then using its apparent log density of 2.04 g/cm3 — and brought salt-bed porosity from 0.33 to 0.011 against NMR 0.026. Independent sub-agents applied the same procedure to three further wells chosen from 75 with calibration data. It diagnosed kerogen in the Bakken shales, halite and an unrepresentable potash bed in the Devonian Prairie Evaporite, and an NMR discrepancy that was not a mineral problem in a Madison limestone. In two wells it rejected an iterate that fitted the logs better but contradicted spectroscopy or cuttings.
evidence_items.title: Inside an Agentic Formation-Evaluation Harness: Skills, Skill-Controlled Loops and a Calibrated Mineral Inversion on Antelope 1-36-25H, Williston Basin

organizations: Service of Infectious Diseases, Department of Medicine, Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Vaudois (CHUV) , Lausanne ,
evidence_items.summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) discourse in infectious disease (ID) has focused on benchmarking large language model chatbots against clinicians, a useful but narrowing inquiry. Agentic AI is a different paradigm: goal-directed systems that pursue clinical objectives over time, integrating data, invoking tools, monitoring results, and adapting without repeated prompting. This Viewpoint defines the anatomy of an agent, situates it within a 3-level framework (predictive, conversational, agentic), and examines how agents could transform 6 domains of ID practice: clinical care, antimicrobial stewardship, clinical microbiology, infection prevention and control, research, and epidemiology and pandemic preparedness. Individual components have proven value; integrated systems remain untested. No validated agentic system has been deployed in clinical ID; error propagation, algorithmic bias, cost, absent validation frameworks, undefined liability, and consequences for the workforce and its training must be addressed first. The ID community has a narrow window to shape these systems before decisions are made without it.
evidence_items.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Infectious Disease Practice

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Chest radiography (CXR) is considered a cost-effective method for the detection of pulmonary tuberculosis (TB). However, current computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems focus primarily on image-level classification, providing limited information on the specific radiological abnormalities underlying their predictions. Here we introduce an expert-curated benchmark, NEP-TB-1.1K, that consists of 1,034 frontal CXRs with 1,735 bounding boxes for two cardinal radiological manifestations, airspace opacity (AO) and pleural effusion (PE). These findings represent radiological abnormalities that may occur in pulmonary TB and overlap with other pulmonary conditions, making their reliable localisation relevant to interpretable chest radiography analysis. We systematically evaluate four representative modern object detection models on this benchmark. These include the attention-centric YOLOv12, the transformer-based Real-Time DEtection TRansformer (RT-DETR), the two-stage Faster R-CNN, and the lightweight SSD-MobileNet. Because diffuse infectious exudates lack sharp radiometric margins, model localization is assessed using both standard (intersection-over-union [IoU] = 0.5) and clinically tolerant (IoU = 0.3) spatial thresholds. RT-DETR ranked first with a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.578 (AO: 0.606, PE: 0.550) at IoU = 0.5, and was followed by YOLOv12 (0.517) and Faster R-CNN (0.514). Relaxed to IoU = 0.3, YOLOv12 achieved the best overall performance with mAP of 0.662 (AO: 0.688, PE: 0.636), showing a significant ability to capture true pathological regions under the boundary ambiguity. Our results show that finding-level localization bridges the gap between generic CAD detections and actionable finding-level triage support, providing a solid basis for granular, interpretable automated thoracic screening.
evidence_items.title: NEP-TB-1.1K: A finding-level benchmark and comparative evaluation of modern deep learning detectors for tuberculosis-related radiographic findings on chest X-ray

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can help cyber-threat-intelligence (CTI) teams interpret unstructured reports, identify potential techniques, and draft response recommendations. The existence of a plausible narrative, however, is not evidence that the threat attribution is warranted or that an automated action is authorised. This conceptual article proposes an evidence-constrained and intervention-ready architecture for LLM-assisted CTI. It develops a bounded critical synthesis of recent research on LLM-assisted CTI and cloud retrieval, established cybersecurity standards, and recent work on action-level accountability. The model passes every interpretation through five gates: source admission, claim extraction, interpretation, decision authorisation, and execution with post-incident review. It specifies a claim-to-evidence ledger, attack-taxonomy version tracking, a calibrated abstention rule, an approval ladder for consequential actions, and a privacy-sensitive audit record. Three hypothetical scenarios (a contaminated threat report, false corroboration across copied sources, and an over-confident automated quarantine) show how a system might fail despite strong benchmark performance. The paper offers evaluation criteria covering support fidelity, mapping accuracy, adversarial robustness, escalation quality, and the time needed to reconstruct and reverse harmful actions. It makes no claim to have trained, deployed, or benchmarked a new CTI model. Its principal contribution is to reframe trustworthy CTI as a question of decision rights: not only whether an AI system recognises a threat, but who may rely on its interpretation, who can authorise an intervention, and who can challenge a damaging classification.
evidence_items.title: From Threat Detection to Decision Rights: Evidence-Constrained Cyber-Threat Intelligence and Accountable Agentic AI

evidence_items.summary: A language-model decoder carries state between decoding steps, and in hardware a wrong state update can leave the current token correct and corrupt the output several tokens later, so a design can pass output tests and still be wrong. AIChipBench asks what LLM coding agents need to build such hardware correctly. Agents implement quantized Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, and Llama 3.2 decoders in synthesizable register-transfer-level (RTL) code against an executable integer reference that specifies the outputs and the stored state at every decoding step. They debug against public tests under fixed budgets; their frozen designs are graded on held-out token sequences, resets, memory stalls, and synthesis, and a second track asks them to speed up a correct design at nearly fixed area. Across 9,136 attempts by four coding agents, the difficulty lies in stored state. Feedback that points to the first state mismatch raises acceptance over output-only feedback in all 12 agent--task cells of a matched study, by 25.0 to 46.9 percentage points, and halves the agent-hours per accepted design. Regraded on new sequences and conditions, 45 of 69 accepted designs fail within the 32 steps their tests required. More than a third of attempts to speed up a correct design end without one. An overall score ranks Sol 5.6 and Fable 5.1 above Astra 6 and Opus 5.5, and both halves of the instances give this order in all 200 random splits. Hardware agents therefore need debugging feedback that exposes stored state, and their benchmarks need final tests well beyond the development cases.
evidence_items.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design

evidence_items.summary: We introduce a reusable generator–jury framework for measuring whether synthetic household fi-nancial narratives support financial assessments consistent with their source records, without requiring human-written reference narratives. The framework uses a two-tier large language model (LLM) jury to derive refer-ence assessments from structured household records. Comparingnarrative-derived assessments with the fixed references enables generation conditions to be evaluated on thesame households. The framework measures how closely narrative-derived assessments match assessments ofthe source records, how this agreement varies across household groups, and how often jury responses can beused in the comparison. evidence_items.summary: Given a reference asset and an instruction such as "remove one armrest," a retriever must find variants that make the edit and preserve the other parts. This search is well established for images but remains underexplored for individual 3D assets. To study this problem, we introduce ShapeQuest and ShapeQuester, a new benchmark and model for edit-conditioned 3D asset retrieval. ShapeQuest's open-source pipeline edits textured meshes through part additions, removals, and material and colour changes. It controls edit granularity across five levels, defined by the fraction of the object's surface area each edit affects. It constructs multiple valid targets when an instruction leaves the choice of part open. A vision-language model judges each edit from views chosen to expose the edited parts, and human raters audit its judgments. ShapeQuest has 87,824 queries in 50 categories and a 50,919-shape gallery with competing edits. To distinguish these variants, ShapeQuester learns retrieval alongside reconstruction of the edited point cloud, with part masks supervising changed and preserved regions. With a frozen pretrained point encoder, ShapeQuester reaches 50.4 operation-macro mAP@10 on the test split, against 47.2 for the fusion baseline with the same inputs and 48.6 for the strongest baseline. Reconstruction adds 6.5 points on the validation split when the point encoder is trained from scratch, including 3.3 from part masks.
evidence_items.title: ShapeQuest: Towards Granularity-Controlled Edit-Conditioned 3D Asset Retrieval

evidence_items.summary: MediaStormBench is a multimodal benchmark for real-world film and television production, with each subset drawn from MediaStorm's day-to-day work. We release its first subset, MediaStormBench-CameraLog (CameraLogBench), on a common foundational task in footage ingest and initial color grading: identifying the Log curve of a clip without metadata. Cameras record Log footage by compressing a wide range of scene light into code values with a vendor-defined logarithmic curve, and color can be restored correctly only once that curve is known. The curve, however, is recorded only in file metadata, easily lost in transcoding and team hand-offs. A colorist then has to try candidate curves one by one against a waveform scope, and a wrong choice shifts the tones and colors of the whole clip. Recovering the curve from the image alone is challenging, because vendor curves cluster tightly in code value and are coupled with unknown exposure. CameraLogBench is built on professionally shot footage and tests whether multimodal models can identify the curve, with a probe that removes the correct option to expose guessing from priors. Because every candidate curve is strictly defined by a published vendor formula, we derive four controls from one implementation of these formulas: graded negatives, synthetic frames of identical scenes, in-context specification digests, and a training-free formula baseline, which together decouple semantic priors from photometric measurement. Across 11 models, real-footage accuracy barely exceeds always guessing the most frequent curve; when the correct option is removed, models almost never abstain, revealing heavy reliance on scene and brand priors. Supplying the vendor specification sharply improves recognition on calibrated charts but hardly helps on natural images without a photometric reference, exposing a gap between reading a specification and measuring pixels.
evidence_items.title: MediaStormBench-CameraLog: Can Multimodal Models Identify a Camera's Log Curve?

evidence_items.summary: Most resource estimates for breaking secp256k1 with Shor's algorithm describe one long run per attempt, and the spacetime volume of that run, its peak number of logical qubits times its Toffoli count, sets its logical-error budget. Eker{\aa}'s tradeoff shrinks each run by using more runs, but how far it can shrink the largest run, and at what circuit cost, has not been determined. We minimize the volume of the largest run while every key is recovered with probability at least 0.99, within ten times the total volume of three runs of H\"aner et al.\ and $2^{40}$ classical operations. We prove that a linear run fixed in advance, which starts its group register at a point and discards its label, reveals at most $\log_2(1+(|S|-1)/r)$ bits about a uniform key, where $|S|$ counts its exponent values and $r$ is the group order. With generic post-processing and the baseline's window costs, splitting alone then shrinks the largest run at most 1.86 times within the budget. To gain more, we make each exponent bit cheaper with windows that share one table point among exponent values related by six symmetries of the curve, on a point-addition core borrowed from the ECDSA.Fail leaderboard. One random scalar and one random start per run give every approximate addition uniform operands, and a bound on each run's outcomes certifies, for every key, a decoder that discards flagged runs. We count every Toffoli gate and every qubit of every run, and each configuration solved all 563 of its pre-registered simulated trials on secp256k1. The best one shrinks the largest run 3.87 times at 8.79 times the baseline's total volume, against 2.81 times for Eker{\aa}'s tradeoff on the same core, and its run is at least 2.6 times smaller than every design of Initio Intelligence.
evidence_items.title: How Small Can a Single Shor Run Be? Limits and Constructions for secp256k1

evidence_items.summary: Learned image captioning metrics are trained and tested on human judgments, so their reported correlation is a claim about generalization. We audit this claim for the three most recent collections of such judgments, Polaris, Nebula, and Spica, matching images at the pixel level. First, test samples reappear in training sets: the Spica training set contains about two-thirds of the Polaris test set, with identical human ratings. Second, controlled retraining shows that duplicates can inflate a metric: for Pearl, the gain is confined to the duplicated samples and grows with every epoch; for DENEB, it stays below one point. The gain depends on the learner and on how often a training set repeats a sample. Third, Kendall's τ over all samples is the sum of two terms, detecting captions with the lowest human score and ranking the others; the first supplies most of the reported correlation and is nearly saturated. The recent test sets cannot order Polos, DENEB and Pearl consistently, and a ridge regression on frozen features matches or exceeds all three. Fourth, we propose a protocol that ranks a learned metric only with a model trained without test samples, reports both terms, and compares metrics by paired tests. Under it, zero-shot vision--language judges rank first on the three recent test sets, and a fine-tuned judge ranks first on the three earlier benchmarks. The same analysis applies to any evaluator learned from human judgments; filter lists and code are released at https://github.com/morninghut/ic-dataset-audit .
evidence_items.title: Do learned image captioning metrics generalize? Auditing duplicated samples in human-judgment benchmarks

rationale: Matched: benchmark, dataset, evaluat, synthetic data
evidence_items.summary: Dataset distillation (DD) aims to compress a large dataset into a small synthetic one that remains effective for training neural networks. Despite its success in supervised learning, DD remains underexplored in self-supervised learning (SSL), where distilled data must preserve the information needed to learn representations that remain consistent across augmentations. To bridge this gap, we introduce Mutual Information Prototype Alignment (MIPA), an efficient SSL dataset distillation approach that optimizes synthetic images to preserve augmentation-invariant information. Specifically, MIPA treats synthetic images as learnable prototypes and uses a frozen encoder to assign real samples to them based on feature similarity. A synthetic dataset that preserves such augmentation invariance should yield stable prototype assignments across multiple augmented views of the same real image. MIPA encourages this by maximizing mutual information between cross-view assignments while avoiding trivial solutions in which all real samples are assigned to only a few synthetic prototypes. Evaluations on image classification benchmarks show that synthetic data generated by MIPA yield higher-quality representations than existing distillation approaches while reducing time and storage demands during distillation.
evidence_items.title: Self-Supervised Dataset Distillation via Mutual Information Maximization

rationale: Matched: benchmark, dataset, evaluat, training data
evidence_items.summary: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector. Experiments on data scale and pipeline coverage further support the value of large, diverse training data. Cross-pipeline evaluations reveal bidirectional and asymmetric generalization. Training on composite forgeries does not necessarily enable detection of their constituent operations in isolation. Our analysis of altered inputs shows that modality masking can increase false alarms and missed detections, and temporal misalignment can raise mean predicted forgery probabilities. Together, these resources provide a foundation for understanding and improving multimodal deepfake detection, with publicly available code and dataset access subject to application and usage terms.
evidence_items.title: Mega-MMDF and DeepfakeBench-MM: Benchmarking Multimodal Deepfake Detection Across Diverse Forgery Pipelines

The original source roadmap establishes the official bilingual topics, while the 819-page visual and scientific mother establishes a durable system of dimensional formulas, reconstructable three-dimensional mathematical diagrams, strong comparators, research gates and independently stoppable future prototypes. The resulting Family 02 turns toward distinctly different epithelial materials: the skin stratum corneum, airway mucus, intestinal mucus and junctions, the ocular tear film, and the difficult question of transferring models across dissimilar organs. We treat their differences as scientific information. A physical endpoint must retain its unit, reference geometry, complete denominator, calibration chain and uncertainty. An attractive surface or a unified algorithm never counts as independent biological evidence. The reasoning framework uses five stages: physical origin, mathematical evolution, counterfactual branching, extreme extrapolation and convergence of evidence. evidence_items.title: STARLI | Skin and Mucosal Biomimetic Barriers | FAMILY 02 F006-F010 | White Rainbow Era | Research Working Edition v1.0  SCIENTIFIC POSITION  This five-flagship research essence is a concise account of proposed physical questions rather than a record of completed laboratory trials. The original source roadmap establishes the official bilingual topics, while the 819-page visual and scientific mother establishes a durable system of dimensional formulas, reconstructable three-dimensional mathematical diagrams, strong comparators, research gates and independently stoppable future prototypes. The resulting Family 02 turns toward distinctly different epithelial materials: the skin stratum corneum, airway mucus, intestinal mucus and junctions, the ocular tear film, and the difficult question of transferring models across dissimilar organs. We treat their differences as scientific information. A physical endpoint must retain its unit, reference geometry, complete denominator, calibration chain and uncertainty. An attractive surface or a unified algorithm never counts as independent biological evidence.  The reasoning framework uses five stages: physical origin, mathematical evolution, counterfactual branching, extreme extrapolation and convergence of evidence. These are stages of disciplined scientific thought; they do not control physical time or compress real experimental duration. Each new hypothesis is prospective, falsifiable and explicitly nonclinical. This booklet does not report measured tissue benefit or establish human efficacy.   FLAGSHIP F006 | Stratum Corneum Biomimetics and Water Retention | 角質層仿生材料與水分保持極限  The core proposition is that corneocyte water binding, intercellular lipid lamellae and humidity-dependent sorption might have a measurable causal relationship with water retention fraction [%]. The smallest bounded demonstration is layered synthetic lipid-corneocyte coupon inside a sealed humidity-gradient diffusion cell. The strongest ordinary reference is matched nonresponsive lipid-polymer laminate and an inert permeation coupon of equal thickness; it should receive the same material mass, observation time, geometry and calibration budget. The experiment does not begin by promising improvement. It begins by asking whether an independent witness can tell the proposed mechanism from edge-seal leakage, uncontrolled specimen mass, hygroscopic contamination or a humidity calibration shift. The main independent evidence is paired gravimetric sorption, calibrated water-vapor flux and independent infrared hydration readout. The stopping condition is mass balance cannot be closed within a preregistered tolerance, or lower water loss coincides with impaired selective transport.   RESEARCH LENS 01: Molecular water-binding versus visual swelling.  Begin with the question of molecular water-binding versus visual swelling. The physically relevant state is not the image of an intact surface but corneocyte water binding, intercellular lipid lamellae and humidity-dependent sorption. In F006, describe the tissue or synthetic analogue, the open transport route, and the conserved quantity before proposing a controller. A plausible rival is already visible: bound-water signal can rise without the same decrease in evaporation. The model must identify which boundary can be measured without reusing the algorithm being tested. Define the operational numerator, denominator, exposed area, time base and unit before choosing samples. For F006, measure water retention fraction [%] with paired gravimetric sorption, calibrated water-vapor flux and independent infrared hydration readout, paired against matched nonresponsive lipid-polymer laminate and an inert permeation coupon of equal thickness. Record an unmodified blank, a empty chamber, repeated instrument zero and span, and every initiated specimen including failed and operator-rescued cases. Preregister the acceptance of missing data; a single photogenic image or internal simulation cannot serve as the endpoint witness. An immediate refutation is that edge-seal leakage, uncontrolled specimen mass, hygroscopic contamination or a humidity calibration shift explains the candidate signal. Expose the empty chamber to the same perturbation, and retire the causal claim if the independent physical reference cannot distinguish it. The precommitted stop is: mass balance cannot be closed within a preregistered tolerance, or lower water loss coincides with impaired selective transport. Do not substitute a correlated proxy for water retention fraction; no result in this prospective volume demonstrates performance on real human tissue.   RESEARCH LENS 08: Repeated desorption and rehydration loops.  Repeated desorption and rehydration loops becomes a mathematical problem only after its unit contract is fixed. Let the perturbations be relative humidity [% RH] and ceramide analogue fraction [fraction], and keep water retention fraction [%] distinct from the illustrative synthetic water retention [%]. Explore an interior stationary point, a cliff near the allowed upper bound, and a nonmonotonic ridge. If several parameter pairs fit one sensor trace, that ambiguity is evidence about identifiability, not a discovery of a universal law. Execute a calibrated factorial grid over relative humidity [% RH] and ceramide analogue fraction [fraction], including center, corners, repeated boundaries and one untouched region. Independently reconstruct water retention fraction [%] at the same sampling times as the reference instrument. Fit both a simple no-interaction surface and an interaction model; release their residual maps, uncertainty intervals and spatial registration errors. The equal-thickness passive polymer follows the identical schedule to reveal an apparatus-only response. Challenge the dimensional model by reversing one gradient, changing the acquisition frequency or exchanging a calibrated area while holding the sample constant. If the model surface changes in the reference channel alone, the purported corneocyte water binding, intercellular lipid lamellae and humidity-dependent sorption is unsupported. A robust mathematical fit is insufficient when edge-seal leakage, uncontrolled specimen mass, hygroscopic contamination or a humidity calibration shift survives. Set aside the fitted relation when the held-out residual or the independent safety witness exceeds its preregistered band.   MATHEMATICAL SIGNATURES FOR F006  1. Gravimetric water-vapor flux: J_w = Delta_m / (A * Delta_t). Units and constraints: J_w [g m^-2 h^-1]; mass [g]; area [m2]; time [h]; mass conserved through sealed cell. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Plot effective area and mass loss at fixed elapsed time; discriminate leakage from tissue transfer. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.  2. Hydration retention percentage: R_w = 100 * (m_t - m_dry)/(m_0 - m_dry). Units and constraints: R_w [%]; all m [g]; m_0 > m_dry; same dry baseline. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Sweep retained mass and dry reference; reject percentage gains from shifted tare. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.  3. Tortuosity-adjusted water diffusivity: D_eff = D_0/(1 + alpha*phi). Units and constraints: D_eff,D_0 [m2 s^-1]; alpha,phi [1]; alpha >= 0; bounded accessible porosity. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Inspect diffusivity against porosity and tortuosity; test whether a leak bypasses serial resistance. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.  4. Lamellar water permeance: P_w = K_w*D_eff/L. Units and constraints: P_w [m s^-1]; K_w [1]; D_eff [m2 s^-1]; L [m]; L > 0; fixed activity and partition model. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Separate K, D and L; identify parameter manifolds with indistinguishable permeance. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.  5. Bound-water depletion time: tau_b = m_bound/(J_w*A). Units and constraints: tau_b [h]; m_bound [g]; J_w [g m^-2 h^-1]; A [m2]; positive flux; fixed area and reservoir definition. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Map reservoir mass against evaporative flux and identify nonstationary boundaries. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.  6. Flux uncertainty propagation: u_J = sqrt((u_m/(A*t))^2 + (J_w*u_A/A)^2 + (J_w*u_t/t)^2). Units and constraints: u_J [g m^-2 h^-1]; u_m [g]; u_A [m2]; u_t [h]; first-order independent errors; positive A,t. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Reveal error ridges created by uncertain active area and time calibration. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.   FLAGSHIP F007 | Airway Mucus Barriers and Particle Exclusion | 呼吸道黏液屏障與微粒阻隔極限  The core proposition is that mucin mesh size, particle surface chemistry and periciliary clearance coupling might have a measurable causal relationship with particle passage fraction [1]. The smallest bounded demonstration is nonclinical airway-mucus-on-chip phantom with replaceable gel and fluorescent inert particles. The strongest ordinary reference is unmodified mucin gel with matched viscosity and a particle-free passive clearance chamber; it should receive the same material mass, observation time, geometry and calibration budget. The experiment does not begin by promising improvement. It begins by asking whether an independent witness can tell the proposed mechanism from particle aggregation, fluorophore quenching, irreversible adsorption to polymer walls or hidden convective bypass. The main independent evidence is independent upstream/downstream particle counts, rheometry and fluorescent-tracer mass closure. The stopping condition is particle mass-count ledger fails or the favorable exclusion suppresses the independently measured clearance pathway.   RESEARCH LENS 01: Mesh-geometry threshold for neutral tracer passage.  Mesh-geometry threshold for neutral tracer passage becomes a mathematical problem only after its unit contract is fixed. Let the perturbations be mucin-network pore diameter [nm] and test particle hydrodynamic diameter [nm], and keep particle passage fraction [1] distinct from the illustrative synthetic particle passage [fraction]. Explore an interior stationary point, a cliff near the allowed upper bound, and a nonmonotonic ridge. If several parameter pairs fit one sensor trace, that ambiguity is evidence about identifiability, not a discovery of a universal law. Execute a calibrated factorial grid over mucin-network pore diameter [nm] and test particle hydrodynamic diameter [nm], including center, corners, repeated boundaries and one untouched region. Independently reconstruct particle passage fraction [1] at the same sampling times as the reference instrument. Fit both a simple no-interaction surface and an interaction model; release their residual maps, uncertainty intervals and spatial registration errors. The no-mucin channel follows the identical schedule to reveal an apparatus-only response. Challenge the dimensional model by reversing one gradient, changing the acquisition frequency or exchanging a calibrated area while holding the sample constant. If the model surface changes in the reference channel alone, the purported mucin mesh size, particle surface chemistry and periciliary clearance coupling is unsupported. A robust mathematical fit is insufficient when particle aggregation, fluorophore quenching, irreversible adsorption to polymer walls or hidden convective bypass survives. Set aside the fitted relation when the held-out residual or the independent safety witness exceeds its preregistered band.   RESEARCH LENS 08: Inlet mixing and shear localization.  Construct a second world in which the headline observation is real but the proposed cause is absent. In that world particle aggregation, fluorophore quenching, irreversible adsorption to polymer walls or hidden convective bypass produces the same direction of change. The counterfactual must receive a real physical arm, not a dismissive paragraph; the nonmoving ciliary phantom is therefore a predeclared antagonist. Explain whether the apparent coupling survives when the device, geometry and observation budget remain unchanged but the active material pathway is disabled. Implement the strongest falsification arm by holding the reference sample unchanged while manipulating particle aggregation, fluorophore quenching, irreversible adsorption to polymer walls or hidden convective bypass. Ask observers blinded to labels to reconstruct the endpoint from raw files. Quantify agreement separately for independent independent upstream/downstream particle counts, rheometry and fluorescent-tracer mass closure; two transformations of the same raw image count as one witness. Reweight all attempted trials, including runs with incomplete extraction. Record an explicit estimate of how much of the nominal difference the engineered rival can explain. If the nonmoving ciliary phantom reproduces the supposed intervention gain, the branch is false even when its statistical fit is excellent. If retention can masquerade as successful exclusion if clearance is lost, discard the tempting story and publish the counterfactual. The critical stop is independent of software: particle mass-count ledger fails or the favorable exclusion suppresses the independently measured clearance pathway. A rival may remain unresolved; mark the mechanism as non-identifiable rather than inventing certainty from two coupled readouts.   MATHEMATICAL SIGNATURES FOR F007  1. Particle passage fraction: f_pass = N_out/N_in. Units and constraints: f_pass [1]; N counts particles; N_in>0; count efficiency independently calibrated. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Sweep particle size and mesh spacing; detect spurious passage caused by optical loss. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.  2. Particle number flux: J_p = N_out/(A*Delta_t). Units and constraints: J_p [particles m^-2 s^-1]; A [m2]; t [s]; fixed observation window and exposed area. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Map passage-rate hotspots as boundary channels open at a corner. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.  3. Stokes-Einstein Brownian diffusion: D_B = k_B*T/(6*pi*eta*r). Units and constraints: D_B [m2 s^-1]; k_B [J K^-1]; T [K]; eta [Pa s]; r [m]; dilute spherical passive particles, Newtonian approximation. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Vary viscosity and radius; mark failure when mucus rheology is non-Newtonian. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.  4. Particle Peclet number: Pe_p = U*L/D_B. Units and constraints: Pe_p [1]; U [m s^-1]; L [m]; D_B [m2 s^-1]; positive D_B; declared advective axis. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Map diffusion-dominated and clearance-dominated regimes without equating the two. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.  5. Residence-time estimate: tau_r = L/U. Units and constraints: tau_r [s]; L [m]; U [m s^-1]; U>0; steady one-dimensional surrogate. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Plot velocity against path length; challenge plug-flow assumptions. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.  6. Absolute exclusion probability: E_p = 1 - f_pass. Units and constraints: E_p [1]; paired counting; bounded f_pass 0..1. Falsifiable 3D geometry: A false-high exclusion ridge appears if the detector selectively misses bound tracers. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.   FLAGSHIP F008 | Intestinal Mucosal Transport and Repair | 腸道黏膜選擇性運輸與修復極限  The core proposition is that mucus turnover, epithelial tight-junction selectivity and transport under microfluidic shear might have a measurable causal relationship with apparent solute permeability [m s^-1]. The smallest bounded demonstration is two-channel intestinal epithelium chip with removable mucus analog and gravimetric tracer recovery. The strongest ordinary reference is matched transwell reference epithelia and acellular microfluidic inserts with equal adsorption budget; it should receive the same material mass, observation time, geometry and calibration budget. The experiment does not begin by promising improvement. It begins by asking whether an independent witness can tell the proposed mechanism from tracer sorption to the chip, flow-induced exposed-area change, epithelial shedding or an electrical-only improvement. The main independent evidence is mass-recovered solute flux, blank-corrected four-electrode TEER and blinded epithelial imaging. The stopping condition is solute mass is unrecoverable, viable reference tissue deteriorates, or TEER rises while independent neutral-tracer flux worsens.   RESEARCH LENS 01: Selective transport after mucus removal.  Construct a second world in which the headline observation is real but the proposed cause is absent. In that world tracer sorption to the chip, flow-induced exposed-area change, epithelial shedding or an electrical-only improvement produces the same direction of change. The counterfactual must receive a real physical arm, not a dismissive paragraph; the recognized intestinal epithelial monolayer is therefore a predeclared antagonist. Explain whether the apparent coupling survives when the device, geometry and observation budget remain unchanged but the active material pathway is disabled. Implement the strongest falsification arm by holding the reference sample unchanged while manipulating tracer sorption to the chip, flow-induced exposed-area change, epithelial shedding or an electrical-only improvement. Ask observers blinded to labels to reconstruct the endpoint from raw files. Quantify agreement separately for independent mass-recovered solute flux, blank-corrected four-electrode TEER and blinded epithelial imaging; two transformations of the same raw image count as one witness. Reweight all attempted trials, including runs with incomplete extraction. Record an explicit estimate of how much of the nominal difference the engineered rival can explain. If the recognized intestinal epithelial monolayer reproduces the supposed intervention gain, the branch is false even when its statistical fit is excellent. If a repair claim needs functional recovery after the perturbation is removed, discard the tempting story and publish the counterfactual. The critical stop is independent of software: solute mass is unrecoverable, viable reference tissue deteriorates, or TEER rises while independent neutral-tracer flux worsens. A rival may remain unresolved; mark the mechanism as non-identifiable rather than inventing certainty from two coupled readouts.   RESEARCH LENS 08: Reversible opening and recovery interval.  Push reversible opening and recovery interval to a deliberately uncomfortable physical limit. Stress the corner that combines high apical flow rate and extreme mucus analog thickness; then repeat after cyclic exposure rather than selecting the first clean trace. The governing approximation solute advection-diffusion coupled to a bounded reversible junctional-state model may fail because a hidden path activates or a local threshold is crossed. A favorable domain average does not excuse a catastrophic local leak, an unmeasured exposure, or an unexplained sensor disagreement. Use boundary tests that cannot be rescued by an operator adjusting a threshold. Apply repeated stress, an intentional instrument drift and a tracer-only no-chip well under matching mass, energy and observation budgets. Report upper-tail failures, not just group means. The most defensible readout is the preregistered apparent solute permeability [m s^-1], jointly checked against blank-corrected TEER [ohm cm2]; if these disagree, preserve both curves and the physical sample provenance. At the extreme corner, explicitly inspect how the denominator and unobserved boundary might reverse the conclusion. A claim of resilience is withdrawn if the sample is functionally degraded despite improved apparent solute permeability [m s^-1]. Stop immediately when solute mass is unrecoverable, viable reference tissue deteriorates, or TEER rises while independent neutral-tracer flux worsens; otherwise let an independent reviewer compare the entire distribution with matched transwell reference epithelia and acellular microfluidic inserts with equal adsorption budget. An extrapolation past the witnessed domain has no empirical authority.   MATHEMATICAL SIGNATURES FOR F008  1. Area-normalized apparent permeability: P_app = (dM_dt)/(A*C_0). Units and constraints: P_app [m s^-1]; dM_dt [mol s^-1]; A [m2]; C_0 [mol m^-3]; sink or corrected donor depletion; A > 0. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Plot loading and active area; detect false advantage from exposure normalization. Units and constraints: TEER [ohm cm2]; R [ohm]; A [cm2]; matched electrode frequency; positive area. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Separate electrode polarization from tight-junction change. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.  3. One-dimensional advective-diffusive flux: J_s = -D_eff*dC_dx + v*C. Units and constraints: J_s [mol m^-2 s^-1]; D_eff [m2 s^-1]; dC_dx [mol m^-4]; v [m s^-1]; one-dimensional mass-conserving transport. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Vary flow and concentration profile; require mass conservation. The diagram remains an illustration unless a reference measurement reconstructs the physical relation.  4. Units and constraints: tau_j [s]; P in [m s^-1]; Delta_t [s]; 00; endpoint identity matched. Falsifiable 3D geometry: Map baseline signal and model mismatch; expose instability near zero reference. Units and constraints: P_i [m s^-1]; J_i [mol m^-2 s^-1]; DeltaC_i [mol m^-3]; identical solute and time convention.
